cases.title: A route back through Form 6
cases.question: Does permission to apply mean a name is back on the roll?
cases.intro: Two applicants moved address, missed enumeration and challenged the route for returning to the roll. Their court order provides a useful starting point for a much wider question.
story: The problem
The two petitioners said their names were deleted after they moved and missed enumeration. They sought a procedure using Form 8 rather than fresh inclusion through Form 6.
The recorded response

The 14 October High Court order copy allows them to submit Form 6 for processing under law. It addresses the first petitioner’s concern about a false-declaration accusation in the circumstances recorded.
The next step
The order does not record the eventual ERO decisions or published entries. The reported wider re-verification drive is a separate administrative development.
cases.established: The court copy records an application route for these two petitioners.
cases.limit: It does not establish completed inclusion or settle the broader challenge to the declaration.
cases.missing: Application receipts, ERO decisions, matched published entries and the signed local re-verification instruction.

cases.title: Applications are the start of the story
cases.question: How many applications became registrations?
cases.intro: An application bulletin and a revised deadline answer different questions. Read them together, then identify the records needed to establish the result.
story: A count of work received
The CEO bulletin reports Form 6, Form 7 and Form 8 applications. Those categories track different requests, rather than one population of restored voters.
A deadline changes
The signed extension is located. Actual Gazette publication remains unverified. A public web page also contains conflicting schedule sections.
The outcome still needs a link
To establish inclusion, a return must connect accepted requests with the resulting roll entries. Aggregate intake figures do not supply that link.
cases.established: The archive contains the signed extension and a CEO application bulletin.
cases.limit: Application totals are neither unique-person counts nor completed restoration counts.
cases.missing: Gazette publication, disposal returns and matched roll supplements.

cases.title: The totals balance. The individual decisions remain open.
cases.question: What does a correct reconciliation prove?
cases.intro: Goa’s signed report gives this investigation a complete draft-to-final equation. It also shows why an accounting result is only one part of an outcome audit.
story: Start with the same populations
Keep the pre-SIR, draft and final rolls distinct. Each is a stock at a different stage, not a count of people wrongly removed.
Reconcile the movement
The draft-to-final equation includes accepted additions and two removal categories. The figures balance against the final count.
Return to the people affected
The separate 97-person discussion concerns applications and reported acceptances. Individual orders and matched supplements are still needed to establish outcomes.
cases.established: The official draft-to-final figures reconcile arithmetically.
cases.limit: A balanced total does not establish the legality of every eligibility decision.
cases.missing: Individual decision files, reasons, appeal outcomes and linked roll entries.

cases.title: Thirteen districts, one reconciliation
cases.question: How far does a district-level check take us?
cases.intro: The final report permits a stronger accounting check than a single statewide headline. A later operational bulletin also changes how an older date anomaly should be read.
story: An earlier timing question
The historical May schedule had a printed-date anomaly. A later operational source narrows that issue; the old dates alone do not establish actual pre-draft notices.
Check every district
All 13 district equations and the four statewide column totals reconcile against the official final-publication report.
Keep the limit in view
Admitted claims and objections are administrative categories. They do not identify a population of people wrongly excluded and later restored.
cases.established: All 13 district equations and statewide column totals reconcile.
cases.limit: The audit checks official arithmetic, rather than individual eligibility or service of notices.
cases.missing: Actual notice-service dates, decision files and person-linked outcomes.

cases.title: The judgment and the individual decision
cases.question: What follows from upholding the SIR framework?
cases.intro: The Bihar judgment establishes the legal starting point. The next task is to distinguish the framework the Court upheld from the correctness of a particular local decision.
story: The framework is challenged
The national debate begins with the intensive revision and its relationship to election law, eligibility and access to remedies.
The Court decides the framework
The May judgment upholds the broad process while placing legal bounds on citizenship-related determinations.
Implementation remains a separate test
A ruling on the framework does not decide every subsequent notice, form version, hearing or exclusion. Those require their own records.
cases.established: The archive contains the May judgment and its legal qualifications.
cases.limit: The holding does not certify every local decision or later implementation.
cases.missing: Case-level notices, hearings, decisions, citizenship referrals and competent-authority outcomes.

cases.title: A safeguard needs a record of its use
cases.question: Were the court-ordered procedures carried through?
cases.intro: The January and February orders supply concrete directions. Testing their effect requires records of the notices, adjudications and entries that followed.
story: The dispute reaches the Court
The proceedings concern how discrepancies and unresolved cases should be handled in West Bengal.
Specific safeguards are directed
The inspected January and February orders provide state-specific directions. They should not be treated as a rewritten national procedure.
The outcome audit is still open
The order text establishes what was directed. Returns and decision records are needed to determine how those directions operated.
cases.established: The January and February primary orders are inspected with locators.
cases.limit: The order texts do not by themselves establish compliance or final individual outcomes.
cases.missing: Notice registers, adjudication returns and operative roll supplements.

cases.title: From a bulk objection to a final decision
cases.question: What happened after Form 7 objections were submitted?
cases.intro: Bulk applications deserve examination. Submission, acceptance, deletion and criminal liability are different events, each requiring its own evidence.
story: Identify the objection
The investigation distinguishes the number of submitted objections from what an ERO eventually did with them.
Check the applicable safeguards
Form 7 limits and scrutiny directions provide a standard to examine. The Karnataka preservation and criminal-proceeding developments remain reported evidence pending authenticated orders.
Trace the transaction
An objection record, notice, response, decision and roll change should be linked before drawing an outcome conclusion. An announced ECINet review does not provide those records.
cases.established: The October Form 7 directions are located; other local proceedings retain their source qualifications.
cases.limit: A submitted objection or a reported stay proves neither wrongful deletion nor guilt or exoneration.
cases.missing: Authenticated local court orders, original objections, transaction history and matched ERO decisions.

cases.title: A deadline corrected, a later order still missing
cases.question: How should an investigation handle a changing schedule?
cases.intro: This case starts with a mistake in our own reporting. The signed original annexure resolves it. A later reported timetable introduces a different source question.
story: We misread the original window
An earlier version alleged an impossible claims deadline. The original signed annexure gave 21 October to 20 November. The allegation was corrected publicly.
A later timetable is reported
The archive adds a subsequent public-broadcaster account. It is kept separate from authentication of the replacement instrument.
Keep the versions distinct
The original May dates remain historical. A later report does not substitute for the signed replacement and any amendments.
cases.established: The original annexure resolves our earlier deadline error.
cases.limit: The later reported timetable remains unconfirmed against its signed replacement instrument.
cases.missing: The signed replacement order and subsequent amendments.
